assessment.nobel_worthiness: A general method for forming aryl C-N bonds that turned a hard transformation into a routine one. Its adoption is visible in countless syntheses, in medicinal chemistry and in industrial process routes. This is exactly the bond-building efficiency I value, and it is clearly chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, broadly applicable ligand-controlled versions in the mid-1990s and made them general. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is an important precursor, but the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize with Kosugi as a possible third.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent use and confirmation. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The 2010 prize for Pd cross-coupling may be seen as having already covered this area, and I am not certain how the committee would weigh that.
Whether Kosugi's priority deserves a laureate slot is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic: ordinary C-H bonds become handles for stereocontrolled and site-selective bond construction. Directing-group, ligand and template control are conceptual advances that shortened synthetic routes and are now used in late-stage functionalization.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand and template-enabled site selectivity), Sanford (Pd and high-valent catalysis) and Hartwig (borylation and C-H functionalization) have distinct and decisive contributions. Daugulis and Smith are also credited, so the three-person cut is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strong, widely replicated, with growing industrial uptake. Some subfields, such as remote meta and para functionalization, are still maturing, but the core is established.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over several mechanistically different approaches, so a three-person cut will leave out important contributors.
Industrial scale-up beyond late-stage diversification is less documented than for cross-coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell pathways under mild conditions and is now routine in synthesis labs and in pharmaceutical discovery. The conceptual novelty is in how it enabled new bond disconnections and merged with organo- and transition-metal catalysis.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 Yoon, MacMillan and Stephenson trio is the usual core, with Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre as important additional contributors. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize, which may weigh against naming him. My list is a reasonable but contestable choice.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of broad adoption and independent confirmation. It is mature, though still evolving.
uncertainties: Attribution is crowded and priority with earlier photochemists such as Kellogg and Fukuzumi is unresolved.
MacMillan's prior prize could argue for a different configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes established a new class of compounds. N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, notably in second-generation metathesis catalysts and in Pd and Ni catalysis, so their impact on how molecules are built is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first stable crystalline NHC in 1991 and Bertrand isolated the earlier stable phosphino-carbene. Nolan is credited for NHC ligand chemistry in catalysis. Bode and Rovis cover NHC organocatalysis, which is a distinct strand.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with thirty years of confirmation and heavy use.
uncertainties: The fundamental discovery and the catalytic application are different achievements that may be recognised differently.
Whether Nolan is more deserving than Bode or Rovis depends on whether the prize emphasises ligands or organocatalysis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide fragments and made total chemical synthesis of proteins practical. It is a molecule-making method at the border of chemistry and biology, and the chemical novelty is clear.
assessment.attribution: Dawson and Kent introduced NCL in 1994, with Kent as the central figure of chemical protein synthesis. Muir's expressed protein ligation extends it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are also credited, so a trio is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent use in protein science and biologics. Industrial adoption is narrower than cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Impact is concentrated in specialist protein chemistry rather than general synthesis.
The allocation between ligation chemistry and semisynthesis is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave general, controlled radical polymerization with defined architectures and low dispersity, and is widely used in materials and industry. The conceptual step of reversible halogen-atom transfer is elegant and transferable.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto-Kamigaito independently reported the method in 1995, and Wang co-authored Matyjaszewski's paper. A trio of the three principal names is plausible. The credit and priority split is a real unresolved question.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed, with commercial products.
uncertainties: RAFT polymerization competes as a conceptually parallel recognition, and the committee might prefer to treat them together or not at all.
Polymer chemistry sits farther from my own expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs show that sterically hindered acid and base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, opening metal-free hydrogenation. The idea is conceptually simple and chemically new.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free reversible H2 activation in 2006, and Erker developed the field extensively, including the intramolecular systems. The two-person credit looks fair.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed conceptually, but practical catalytic scope and industrial use are still limited compared with transition-metal catalysis.
uncertainties: Synthetic impact so far is less than for the methods ranked above, so recognition may be somewhat early.
Priority relative to earlier related main-group work is not something I can verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bergman's 1982 oxidative addition of alkane C-H bonds at iridium was a landmark that proved saturated hydrocarbons can be activated intermolecularly by a soluble metal complex. It underpins later C-H functionalization, but it was a stoichiometric mechanistic demonstration rather than a practical method.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit lists only Bergman, though Graham and Jones reported related work at about the same time. A single-laureate prize would likely be contested on attribution.
assessment.maturity: Historically confirmed and foundational. The practical catalytic payoff came through later work, which makes B034 the more natural vehicle.
uncertainties: Overlap with B034 means one prize might cover both, and I am unsure of the full priority picture with Graham and Jones.
